reference_diagnosis.name: Episodic ataxia type 2 (CACNA1A)
reference_diagnosis.basis: Hours-long attacks triggered by stress/exercise/alcohol, interictal downbeat nystagmus, vermian atrophy, AD family history, acetazolamide response, CACNA1A variant.

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Episodic vertigo with headache; mother with migraine
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Interictal downbeat nystagmus and vermian atrophy are not explained
EA1 attacks last seconds–minutes, triggered by sudden movement, with interictal myokymia, not nystagmus
Late-onset progressive ataxia rather than discrete attacks at 12; allelic with EA2

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Episodic neurological symptoms in a young adult
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Stereotyped attacks since age 12, interictal downbeat nystagmus, no demyelination on MRI

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Weekend heavy drinking; superior vermian atrophy is typical of alcohol damage
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Attacks began at 12, before drinking; discrete hours-long attacks with downbeat nystagmus and a family history fit EA2; alcohol here is a trigger

held_out_evidence.result: Mother's 'migraines' include episodes of ataxia lasting hours; she carries the same variant.

cant_miss.why_required: Posterior fossa lesions need specific treatment
cant_miss.status_in_record: addressed: vermian atrophy only, no demyelination or mass

cant_miss.condition: Treatable acquired ataxia (vitamin E, B12, coeliac, anti-GAD)

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable; considered in any unexplained movement disorder, most strongly under 50
cant_miss.status_in_record: low risk: discrete episodic attacks are not a Wilson pattern; not tested, optional

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Accepting vestibular migraine without explaining interictal nystagmus and vermian atrophy
Confusing EA1 and EA2 attack duration and triggers
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Recommending treatment as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Citing literature that does not exist or does not support the specific claim
Asserting case facts that are not in the case record
Attributing the vermian atrophy to alcohol without addressing that attacks began at age 12
clinician_review_notes: Clinical review 2026-10-17 (pending Wiki sign-off). Classic EA2. Added MS and alcohol-related cerebellar damage as hypotheses (superior vermian atrophy is also typical of alcohol), cant_miss, one red flag and expected behaviour.
expected_system_behavior: EA2 should rank first. The system should explain why vestibular migraine does not account for interictal downbeat nystagmus and vermian atrophy, separate EA2 from EA1 by attack length and interictal signs, link the mother's episodes and the grandfather's late gait problem to a CACNA1A family spectrum, and suggest CACNA1A testing with acetazolamide response as supportive.
